'''Games influenced by Star Wars CCG''' reuse the rules of Decipher's ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game (SWCCG) or borrow its mechanics. Decipher built ''[[WARS Trading Card Game|WARS]]'' (2004) on the SWCCG game system. Players Committee designer [[Ryan Jellison]] says the ''My Little Pony'' Collectible Card Game (2013) copied SWCCG's battle destiny.<ref name="jellison" /><ref name="icv2-4495" />

== Decipher games ==
=== Young Jedi ===
''[[Young Jedi]]'' (1999) was a simpler ''Phantom Menace'' game for younger players.<ref name="tfn-kallenbach" /> SWCCG designers [[Tom Braunlich]] and [[Rollie Tesh]] said destiny numbers, location-based play and depleting the opponent's Force were hallmarks "that will be in all of our games".<ref name="rfd16" /> Designer [[Chuck Kallenbach]] said "a real 'bridge' from Young Jedi to SWCCG was not intended."<ref name="tfn-kallenbach" />

=== Jedi Knights Trading Card Game ===
Kallenbach designed the ''[[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]]'' (2001) with [[Tom Lischke]]. Asked whether it drew on Decipher's best mechanics, he said: "It was filled with stuff that Tom and I liked."<ref name="tfn-kallenbach" />

=== WARS Trading Card Game ===
After Lucasfilm moved the ''Star Wars'' card game license to Wizards of the Coast, Decipher kept its game mechanics. Lucasfilm had the right to license them for the new game but chose not to.<ref name="icv2-983" /><ref name="rfd-holland" /> In 2004 Decipher announced a game "built on the mechanics Decipher developed for its best-selling Star Wars CCG", set in its own universe.<ref name="icv2-4495" /> It launched as ''[[WARS Trading Card Game|WARS]]'' on 6 October 2004.<ref name="icv2-4824" /> [[Warren Holland]] said he "got thousands and thousands of emails from people that wanted us to bring back the Star Wars mechanics".<ref name="dwr3" />

== My Little Pony Collectible Card Game ==
[[File:MLP CCG The Brave and the Bold CN119.jpg|thumb|right|200px|''The Brave and the Bold'' (''Canterlot Nights'', 2014).]]
[[File:Premiere-L-giftofthementor.gif|thumb|right|200px|[[Gift Of The Mentor]] (Premiere, 1995).]]
Enterplay published the ''My Little Pony'' Collectible Card Game from 2013. Its lead designer was Darrell Hardy.<ref name="mlp-rules" /> Enterplay's founder and president, [[Dean Irwin]], had been Decipher's sales director, "responsible for all their global sales".<ref name="icv2-irwin" />

Jellison said the game "was designed by people who worked at Decipher". He pointed to its mechanics: "you draw battle destiny in the game ... and there's a destiny number on it."<ref name="jellison" />

In a ''My Little Pony'' faceoff, each player adds "the power of the top card of your deck" to the power of their cards in the contest.<ref name="mlp-rules" /> Players "ignore everything on the card except its power value", so the printed power number works like an SWCCG destiny number.<ref name="mlp-rules" /> A tie means both players flip again.<ref name="mlp-rules" />

Jellison compared the game's pair cards to {{CardLink|Gift Of The Mentor|Premiere-L-giftofthementor.gif}}, which adds two battle destiny when Luke and Obi-Wan or Yoda battle together: "It's also destiny five. It's like a direct copy."<ref name="jellison" /> ''The Brave and the Bold'' flips one additional card when Rainbow Dash or Applejack is in the faceoff, and two when both are. Its flip value is 5.<ref name="ponyhead" /> The ''Premiere'' set's pair cards, such as ''Team Effort'', have power 4.<ref name="ponyhead" />

== Not built on SWCCG ==
Wizards of the Coast's ''[[Star Wars Trading Card Game]]'' (2002) used "all new game mechanics".<ref name="icv2-983" /> Holland called it "totally incompatible with any of our existing games".<ref name="icv2-983" /> Decipher's ''[[The Lord of the Rings Trading Card Game]]'' (2001) shared designers with SWCCG. Designer Tom Lischke said "we have gone out of our way to do a lot of things differently".<ref name="tor-lischke" />

== Borrowing into SWCCG ==
The [[Players Committee]] designs new virtual cards. Jellison said some of them borrow from other games: "There are Pokemon inspired cards ... There are also Game of Thrones, and Lord of the Rings", and "it's really easy to borrow from My Little Pony, honestly."<ref name="jellison" />
